creator_hub_you_are_the_automation_imple:
You are the automation implementer. Write an implementation-ready plan for a weekly load report using Orider's public recipe docs.

Goal: every Monday morning, read the last 7 days from the Orider Personal Data API and create both a private HTML report and an aggregate Notion summary.
Reference paths: create API keys at /en/settings/developer; API guide is docs/PERSONAL_DATA_API-en.md; the formal API contract is Swagger UI /api/v1/docs or OpenAPI YAML /api/v1/docs/openapi.yaml; recipe docs are docs/recipes/weekly-load-report-en.md; report template is docs/recipes/report-template-en.md; runnable example is examples/recipes/weekly-load-report/weekly-load-report.mjs.
API contract check: confirm the X-API-Key header, endpoint paths, request/response schemas, content types, and error codes in Swagger/OpenAPI. Do not invent endpoints or response fields from markdown docs alone.
Required scopes: default to Orider activities:read and fitness:read only. Add streams:read only when the rider explicitly wants private HTML route/map thumbnails, then call the route thumbnail endpoint documented in Swagger/OpenAPI. Notion should only be allowed to create pages in the target database.
Values the user must provide: ORIDER_API_KEY, NOTION_TOKEN, NOTION_DATABASE_ID, timezone, Monday run time.
Outputs: weekly-load-report.html, weekly-load-summary.json, weekly-load-public-summary.txt, and a Notion row.
Report sections: top readout, KPI cards, 7-day daily load bar chart, previous-7-day comparison, key-session summary, and next action.
Never store: location, route coordinates, start/end areas, detailed activity names, detailed HR/power streams, or API keys.
Output format: file structure, API call order, data transform functions, HTML template structure, Notion property schema, n8n or GitHub Actions runner, environment variables, error handling, test steps, and done criteria.
Important: if an endpoint or response field is not documented in Swagger/OpenAPI, mark it as needs confirmation instead of inventing it.

creator_hub_you_are_the_automation_imple:
You are the automation implementer. Write an implementation-ready plan that connects the Orider Personal Data API to a private Slack recovery alert.

Goal: every morning, check recent training load and send a Slack DM only when overload conditions match.
Reference paths: create API keys at /en/settings/developer; API guide is docs/PERSONAL_DATA_API-en.md; the formal API contract is Swagger UI /api/v1/docs or OpenAPI YAML /api/v1/docs/openapi.yaml.
API contract check: confirm the X-API-Key header, endpoint paths, request/response schemas, content types, and error codes in Swagger/OpenAPI.
Required scopes: use only Orider activities:read. Slack should only be able to send a private DM or webhook message.
Values the user must provide: ORIDER_API_KEY, SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL or SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_USER_ID, timezone, daily run time.
Rules: alert when 2 of the last 3 days were hard or the last 7 days of load are 30% above the rider's normal baseline. If no baseline exists, collect baseline data for the first 2 weeks instead of alerting.
Message content: today's suggested intensity, one-line reason, and a 7-day aggregate summary only.
Never send: location, routes, activity names, detailed heart-rate values, or automatic team-channel posts.
Output format: execution flow, Slack setup, API call order, pseudocode or n8n nodes, duplicate-alert prevention, test steps, and done criteria.
Important: if an endpoint or response field is not documented in Swagger/OpenAPI, mark it as needs confirmation instead of inventing it.

creator_hub_you_are_the_n8n_automation_i:
You are the n8n automation implementer. Write an implementation-ready n8n workflow that uses the Orider Personal Data API to draft a monthly riding badge and email it to me first.

Goal: at 9 AM on the first day of each month, create public-safe badge copy from last month's riding aggregates and email it to me.
Reference paths: create API keys at /en/settings/developer; API guide is docs/PERSONAL_DATA_API-en.md; the formal API contract is Swagger UI /api/v1/docs or OpenAPI YAML /api/v1/docs/openapi.yaml.
API contract check: confirm the X-API-Key header, endpoint paths, request/response schemas, content types, and error codes in Swagger/OpenAPI.
Required scopes: use only Orider activities:read. The email node sends only to my address.
Values the user must provide: ORIDER_API_KEY, email/SMTP account settings, recipient email, timezone.
Calculated fields: last month's total distance, elevation, ride count, and longest ride distance.
Example public copy: 'June: 18 rides · 642 km · 7,820 m climbed · longest 112 km'.
Do not auto-publish: do not post to a blog, profile, or social channel automatically; the user reviews the email and posts manually.
Output format: n8n Cron, HTTP Request, Set, and Email node settings, each node's input/output, retry behavior, sample JSON, test steps, and done criteria.
Important: if an endpoint or response field is not documented in Swagger/OpenAPI, mark it as needs confirmation instead of inventing it.

creator_hub_you_are_the_web_automation_i:
You are the web automation implementer. Write an implementation-ready server/automation design and frontend code for a public Orider profile badge on a personal website.

Goal: never expose the API key in the browser. Once per day, read Orider monthly aggregates, update public JSON, and render that JSON as a small badge on the site.
Reference paths: create API keys at /en/settings/developer; API guide is docs/PERSONAL_DATA_API-en.md; the formal API contract is Swagger UI /api/v1/docs or OpenAPI YAML /api/v1/docs/openapi.yaml.
API contract check: confirm the X-API-Key header, endpoint paths, request/response schemas, content types, and error codes in Swagger/OpenAPI.
Required scopes: use Orider activities:read, or a more limited monthly aggregate scope if OpenAPI/the guide provides one.
Values the user must provide: ORIDER_API_KEY, public JSON storage location, site path for the badge, timezone.
Public JSON schema: include only month, distanceKm, elevationM, rideCount, and updatedAt.
Exclude: routes, start/end areas, activity names, detailed heart-rate/power values, and API keys.
Output format: recommended architecture, GitHub Actions or server-function example, environment variables, public JSON example, frontend badge component, cache/error handling, test steps, and done criteria.
Important: if an endpoint or response field is not documented in Swagger/OpenAPI, mark it as needs confirmation instead of inventing it.
